### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 910306b632bfeb4a6d12a03d6ab489fd1a3d6128` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7fc680e827bba18c18f8f791885323e72ca8a55f` — the merge of head `c56f66f4efc04d4e00411e35f0ff6e02463e962a` into base `910306b632bfeb4a6d12a03d6ab489fd1a3d6128`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c56f66f4efc04d4e00411e35f0ff6e02463e962a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: brief 6976945886; card #35138 (body and all 10 comments, among them claim 6975089907, W0 decisions 6975318215 and os-dev report 6976907593); PR #35185 (body and comments); the full diff against merge-base `7d8dcf693a` (3 commits, 7 files, +292/−11); the changeset; and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only.

Face: the committed file list is one changeset and six files under `packages/mcp/src/`. It touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path. `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` decides no face from the paths and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `yes (widening)`. So this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is still running.** 50 check-runs: 23 success, 16 skipped, 11 in progress, 0 failure. Still running: `Test Core` (7 of 10 shards), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`. Complete and green: `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (which carries the NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), `Lint · ESLint`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI` and `Live E2E UI`. I judge on what is complete. The seat must see the 11 in-progress runs finish green on this head before landing. The 2 failures on the earlier head `d85434872f` are its aggregate jobs, which ran after 19 cancelled runs when the head moved. They are not readings of this head.
- **The probe and `truncated` on `query_records`: widened, right.** The handler asks the bridge for `page + 1` rows. `servedQueryPage` serves the first `page` rows and adds `truncated: true` only when the extra row came back. The member is absent otherwise, never `false`, so a page holding every matching row (exactly `limit` rows included) answers the same keys as before. Where the bridge answers `hasMore`, it is restated from the probe: true exactly when more rows came back than the page holds. That is right: the door counted `hasMore` against the widened read. `total` is untouched, and on the HTTP door it is a count that does not depend on the limit (`findData`, `protocol-data-crud.ts` around line 790). A result that is not a plain object with a `records` array is passed through unchanged. That matches the `withDelegationNotice` posture, which still runs after it.
- **The fallback where the read window would refuse the probe: sound, and no full page is newly refused.** `queryPageProbeFits` mirrors the two refusals in `planQueryReadWindow` (`packages/types/src/query-read-limits.ts` at `origin/main`): a `limit` over `maxPageSize`, and `offset` plus `limit` over `rowBudget`. It skips the probe in exactly the cases where `page + 1` would be refused and `page` would not. The tool always sends a `limit`, so the planner's default-page arms are never reached. A page that was itself over the window was refused before this PR and is refused the same way now. Where the probe is skipped, `truncated` comes from the door's counted `hasMore`. On the HTTP door that is `findData`'s counted arm. On the stdio door it is the new count below. `resolveQueryReadLimits()` runs inside the handler's `try`, the same reader `deleteRecordsCap` already uses, so a misconfigured variable surfaces as the door's error, as it does on the data door. The pin with `OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE` equal to the page covers both doors: no probe is sent, a capped page is flagged and a whole page is not.
- **The stdio bridge's page facts: right.** A paged read now runs `engine.count(object, { where }, { context })`. I read the count path at `origin/main` (`engine-count-aggregate.ts`): `mergeReadContext` takes the third argument's `context`, and the read filters are applied through the middleware chain on the count AST, as for `find`. So the count runs as the caller, under the same `where`, after the exposure, body-hash and sort refusals the read already passed. `total` is the match total, and `hasMore` is true when `offset` plus the rows served is below the count, which is `findData`'s formula. If the count throws, `total` is omitted and `hasMore` is answered from the page alone. That is the data door's `$count=false` arm (a full page here answers `hasMore: true`; the door tests for exactly `limit` rows, and the two agree because a page cannot exceed its limit). An unpaged read keeps `total: records.length`, gains `hasMore: false`, and runs no count. Before this PR, a capped stdio page answered `total` equal to the page length with no `hasMore`. The only change to stdio `total` is that a paged read now reports a counted number, or none. `hasMore` is a new member.
- **The tool description: right.** It now says the answer is one page of at most `limit` rows, that a `truncated` page must not be summed, counted or ranked as if whole, and to read on with `offset` or use `aggregate_records` "where it is offered". That hedge is correct: `aggregate_records` is registered only when the bridge has `aggregate`.
- **Built entry of `@objectstack/mcp`: nothing removed, renamed or narrowed.** The `exports` map has only `.`. `queryPageProbeFits` and `servedQueryPage` are module-private. `McpDataBridge.query` keeps its signature and its `Promise of unknown` return. `createStdioDataBridge` keeps its signature. The answer body is untyped, and the claim's reading holds: the spec types only the `source` block of this result (`object-query-source.zod.ts`), so no spec type changes. Both `bridge.query` callers in `delete_records` read rows only, never `total` or `hasMore`. No input a caller could send before is refused now.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. The new stdio read is an engine `count` under the caller's `where`, which the driver runs as a count. The HTTP door already counts in `findData`, so it gains no read. The probe adds one row to the page read. The cost noted in the PR body's Acceptance notes is real: on stdio, `delete_records`' selection reads go through the same `query` member, so they also run the count. A full filter selection is then counted twice, once by `query` and once by the existing aggregate count. That is one extra count per stdio delete call, with no materialisation. It is acceptable as declared.
- **The helper move `d85434872f..c56f66f4ef`: a pure move.** Its diff is 20 lines out and the same 20 lines in. `withDelegationNotice` moves below the two new helpers, and no line changes. So the PR body's readings at `d85434872f` hold for this head's code.

Findings:

- **N1 (nit): where the door answers a page-local `total`, it now counts the probe row.** Two paths answer a `total` that was not counted. One is the `callData('query')` engine fallback when no protocol service is registered (`action-execution.ts`, `total: all.length`). The other is `findData`'s count-failure degrade (`pageOffset + records.length`). On a capped page, both now answer `total` as one more than the rows served, beside `truncated: true`. Before this PR, they answered the page length with no flag. Neither number is a count, and the new answer is no less true: it is still a lower bound, and the flag now says the page is partial. But `servedQueryPage` restates `hasMore` from the probe and leaves `total` alone, and neither the PR body nor the changeset says so. No contract effect.
- **N2 (nit): no pin shows that the stdio count carries the caller's filter.** The counted-total pin calls `bridge.query(OBJECT, { limit: 3 })` and asserts `count` was called with `{}`. If the count dropped `where`, all 11 pins would stay green, and ablation A3 does not cover that mutation. The code is right today, as read above. A pin with a `where` would hold the changeset's "counted under the same filter" sentence.
- **N3 (nit): one corner flags a page that may be whole.** When the read window refuses the probe and the stdio count also fails, `hasMore` comes from the page alone. So an exactly-full last page answers `truncated: true`. The description says the flag means "more records match". The error is in the safe direction, because it only discourages summing. It is reachable only where both conditions hold.
- **N4 (nit): the MCP tools page does not name the new member.** `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx:272` says list queries "are capped at 50 rows per page by default". It does not say that a capped page now answers `truncated: true`. The Docs Drift Check confirms that no hand-written page names the member. Prose only.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/35138-query-records-truncated.md`: right.** It bumps `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`. That is the only published package the diff moves; the tests are not published. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says that `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and that a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. CI `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** It is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and the arm is from the closed pair. An answer member present only when true, a new `hasMore` on the stdio answer, and a counted stdio `total` in place of a page length are additions and corrections. No accepted input is refused, and no member is removed or renamed. The claim 6975089907 and amendment 6975318215 declared `Clause-②: yes` for PR 1.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The result type stays local to `packages/mcp`.
- **Changeset prose, checked against the diff: right.**
  - "asks for one row more than the page; when that row comes back, it serves the page and adds `truncated: true` … present only when true … exactly `limit` rows included, is unchanged": this matches `servedQueryPage`, the A1 and A2 ablations and the exact-limit pins.
  - "tells a model not to sum, count or rank a truncated page … read on with `offset` or use `aggregate_records` for totals": this matches the description text. The description also adds "where it is offered".
  - "a paged read is counted under the same filter, as the caller … Before, a capped stdio page answered `total` equal to the page length. If the count fails, `total` is left out and is never estimated": true. The filter half is unpinned (N2).
  - "When the host's read window … would refuse the extra row, the page is read as asked, and the door's counted `hasMore` decides `truncated`": true, as read in ①.
- **The PR body cites readings at the pre-move head `d85434872f`.** The move is pure (①), so the readings carry over to this head's code. The changeset is the same file at both heads.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, the probe is conditional, not unconditional: answered and right. It is a measured correction of W0's "from a limit+1 probe". Without it, a host with `OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE` equal to the MCP page would refuse every full-page read. The fallback is sound (①).
- Deviation, three pre-existing test files changed: answered.
  - The two preservation pins (`unknown-argument-keys`, 3 to 4; `mcp-server-runtime.http`, 5 to 6) assert the limit the bridge receives. The page served is unchanged, and the new pins assert it.
  - The stdio engine-read census gains `count(object): 1`. That is the new site, and the comment beside it says what it reads: a number, under the `where` the earlier refusals judged.
- Deviation, the NOT-MEASURED gate `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, needs every package's `dist`): answered. CI `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which carries it, succeeded on this head.
- Deviation, the helper move after an overlap with #35179: answered. The move is pure (①). The dev reports `overlap-check` clean against #35179 and #35186 at this head. The merge queue re-tests the merge result.
- Deviation, the PR body is not updated after the move: process only, answered in ②.
- Out-of-scope note, `findData`'s page-local `total` when `engine.count` throws: answered. It is a deliberate degrade, documented at `protocol-data-crud.ts` ("degrade to a page-local total rather than failing the list"), outside this PR's file surface. It is recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes, and not filing it is right under the filing gate: no defect with a public repro. Its interaction with the probe is N1.
- Acceptance note, every paged stdio `bridge.query` now runs one count, `delete_records` included: answered in ① under SQL push-down.
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), assignee `os-warren`, so no extra author note is owed. All four findings are nits, so this is the final round unless the head moves for a reason other than prose. The seat must confirm that the 11 in-progress runs finish green on this head before landing (①).
